mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the primary nutritional mode of plants from that of animals?

options.A: Plants are autotrophic, obtaining carbon from CO₂, whereas animals are heterotrophic, obtaining carbon from organic food.
options.B: Plants are heterotrophic, obtaining carbon from organic food, whereas animals are autotrophic, obtaining carbon from CO₂.
options.C: Both plants and animals are autotrophic, using sunlight as the sole energy source.
options.D: Both plants and animals are heterotrophic, relying on external organic matter for carbon.

mcqs.answer: Plants are autotrophic, obtaining carbon from CO₂, whereas animals are heterotrophic, obtaining carbon from organic food.
mcqs.explanation: Plants synthesize their own organic compounds using CO₂ and sunlight (autotrophy), while animals must ingest organic material to obtain carbon (heterotrophy). Options B, C, and D incorrectly describe the nutritional modes.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares a cellular feature of plant cells with that of animal cells?

options.A: Both plant and animal cells possess rigid cell walls made of cellulose.
options.B: Plant cells contain chloroplasts, while animal cells lack chloroplasts.
options.C: Animal cells have a large central vacuole, whereas plant cells do not.
options.D: Plant cells completely lack lysosomes, while animal cells contain many.

mcqs.answer: Plant cells contain chloroplasts, while animal cells lack chloroplasts.
mcqs.explanation: Chloroplasts are the site of photosynthesis and are present only in plant (and some algal) cells. Animal cells do not have chloroplasts. Options A, C, and D describe features that are either incorrect or not exclusive to one kingdom.

mcqs.question: Which of the following organisms best illustrates the classification of multicellular eukaryotes based on body organization?

options.A: Escherichia coli – a prokaryotic unicellular bacterium
options.B: Moss (a bryophyte) – a multicellular eukaryotic plant with differentiated tissues
options.C: Amoeba proteus – a unicellular eukaryote lacking tissue differentiation
options.D: Saccharomyces cerevisiae – a unicellular fungal yeast

mcqs.answer: Moss (a bryophyte) – a multicellular eukaryotic plant with differentiated tissues
mcqs.explanation: Mosses are multicellular eukaryotes that possess organized tissues, fitting the body‑organization criteria for the plant kingdom. The other options are either prokaryotic or unicellular, lacking the multicellular organization required for this classification.

mcqs.question: A student observes a green, multicellular organism that performs photosynthesis, has cell walls composed of cellulose, and stores starch in plastids. To which kingdom does this organism belong?
mcqs.explanation: The described features—photosynthetic pigments, cellulose cell walls, and starch storage in plastids—are hallmark characteristics of the kingdom Plantae. Animals lack cell walls and photosynthetic ability; fungi have chitin walls; protists are a diverse group not defined by these specific traits.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the kingdom Animalia reflects a common misconception?

options.B: Animals have cell walls made of cellulose.
options.C: Animals are heterotrophic and obtain organic nutrients from other organisms.
options.D: Animals possess specialized nervous tissue for rapid response.

mcqs.answer: Animals have cell walls made of cellulose.
mcqs.explanation: Animals do not have cell walls; they are bounded only by a plasma membrane. The statement about cellulose cell walls is a misconception. Options A, C, and D are accurate descriptions of animal characteristics.

mcqs.question: A green plant is kept in complete darkness for an extended period, preventing photosynthesis. Which nutritional mode will the plant adopt to survive?

options.A: It will continue as an autotroph, using stored reserves without any external source.
options.B: It will become heterotrophic by absorbing organic nutrients from the surrounding medium.
options.C: It will switch to a mixotrophic mode, combining limited photosynthesis with external organic intake.
options.D: It will ultimately die because typical green plants cannot switch to heterotrophy.

mcqs.answer: It will ultimately die because typical green plants cannot switch to heterotrophy.
mcqs.explanation: Most green, non‑parasitic plants lack mechanisms to obtain organic carbon from the environment; without light they cannot perform photosynthesis and eventually die. Options A, B, and C describe abilities that are not present in typical autotrophic plants.

mcqs.question: Which pair correctly matches a cellular feature with the kingdom in which it is found?

options.A: Cell wall composed of cellulose – Kingdom Animalia

mcqs.explanation: Chloroplasts are the photosynthetic organelles characteristic of plant cells. Animal cells lack them, fungi have cell walls of chitin, and peptidoglycan is a feature of bacterial cell walls, not plant cells. Therefore, option B is the only correct match.

mcqs.question: In the five‑kingdom system, which characteristic most effectively distinguishes the kingdom Animalia from the kingdom Plantae?

options.A: Presence of chlorophyll in the cells
options.C: Presence of true tissues and the absence of cell walls

mcqs.answer: Presence of true tissues and the absence of cell walls
mcqs.explanation: Animals are characterized by true (organized) tissues and lack rigid cell walls, whereas plants possess cell walls made of cellulose. Chlorophyll and photosynthesis are plant traits, and starch storage in plastids is also typical of plants. Hence, option C is the key distinguishing feature.
